original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kummer-sequence}
If $n\in \mathcal{O}_S^*$ then
$$
0 \to
\mu_{n, S} \to
\mathbf{G}_{m, S} \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n}
\mathbf{G}_{m, S} \to 0
$$
is a short exact sequence of sheaves on both the small and
big \'etale site of $S$.

stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

On the small or big étale site of a scheme $S$, $\mathbf G_{m,S}(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times)$ is the *units sheaf*, and $\mu_{n,S}(U)=\{u\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^\times):u^n=1\}$ the *$n$th roots of unity* sheaf (representable by the group scheme $\mu_n$). The notation $n\in\mathcal O_S^\times$ means the image of the positive integer $n$ is a unit in the structure sheaf **everywhere on $S$**. A short exact sequence of sheaves means the final map is locally surjective in that site, not necessarily surjective on each group of global sections.

If $n\in \mathcal{O}_S^*$ then
$$
0 \to
\mu_{n, S} \to
\mathbf{G}_{m, S} \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n}
\mathbf{G}_{m, S} \to 0
$$
is a short exact sequence of sheaves on both the small and
big \'etale site of $S$.

**Precise scope:** The last power map G_m→G_m is a **surjection of étale sheaves**, shown by an étale **finite locally free** cover adjoining an nth root of a unit (derivative nT^{n−1} invertible). If n is not invertible this exactness can fail in étale topology; only fppf/syntomic version remains valid without inversion.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves Kummer short exact sequence 0→μ_n→G_m→G_m→0 on both big and small étale sites only for n invertible on S; last map is locally surjective, not necessarily surjective on global units.
